To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of tense is not a static phenomenon; (2) the use of tenses in texts can be analyzed in terms of their deictic center; (3) tense switching is a means of making the moment of writing coincide with the moment of reading; (4) tense switching creates an energy that makes texts dynamic; and (5) the concept of disentanglements helps to understand how some elements of a text live on and some do not.
